summary: Clarify cross-layer refill timing and propose burst rebalancing for webhook-heavy dedicated pool
description:
Issue summary:
Customer (ACME Robotics) reports frequent 429s for webhook callback and background cleanup traffic after moving to a dedicated pool. They see repeated short bursts of rejects that correlate with health-check probes from an edge proxy plus periodic background workers.

Impact:
- Intermittent 429s observed for webhook callbacks (high priority for customer) causing delayed processing of telemetry and missed webhook retries.
- Affects production fleet in us-west primarily; some traffic routed to us-east sees correlated soft-throttles.

Environment:
- Dedicated pool: ACME-dedicated-1 (monthly reserved GPUs)
- Prod region: us-west primary, failover to us-east
- Models: redwood/llama-2-13b for transforms, reranker for small ranking tasks

Observed behavior:
- Short 429 waves lasting 30-90s during scheduled background flusher runs and edge health probes.
- Console shows burst_credit depleted on tenant for those windows; console credit chart shows refill pulses that don’t seem to align with edge refill timestamps.

Expected behavior:
- Background/health probes should be isolated from interactive webhook pool or consume only a separate burst budget so interactive calls remain available.

Steps to reproduce (as described by customer):
1) Customer schedules nightly flusher (10k objects) to run every 5 minutes across backfill workers.
2) Edge proxy performs a rolling health-check sweep every 60s across worker instances.
3) During the flusher sweep, webhooks experience 429s; customer captured timing and traces.

Relevant logs/observations provided by customer:
- Example request IDs: rq_6a9f2b, rq_6a9f3c, rq_6a9f7d (timestamps 2026-03-09T02:34:10Z - 02:34:58Z)
- Console snapshots attached in support portal (heatmap of refill vs depletion)
- Customer observes that after a config change to shorten refill epoch in their edge proxy, 429 frequency increased.

Notes on rate config the customer is using:
- Tenant-level sustained rate + separate short-window burst credits
- Webhooks and background flushers use same API key and therefore share token bucket accounting
- Edge proxy reuses persistent HTTP/2 connections to multiple routes

Customer request:
- Clarify how refill epochs are scheduled between edge and origin accounting layers and whether edge health-checks can double-count.
- Recommend configuration changes to preserve webhook availability while allowing background flushes to run.
investigation_notes:
Initial triage by support: confirmed pattern of short bursts aligning to flusher + health-check timing. Hypothesis: health-checks from edge open additional multiplexed streams that cause extra token accounting on short window refill boundary (edge and origin both apply refill accounting in a way that misaligns the effective epoch).

What we looked at:
- Queried rate-limiter logs for tenant ACME (time range 2026-03-09 02:30-03:00 UTC) — observed refill pulses at 02:30:00 and token_count drops at 02:30:59; multiple connection IDs show preflight and keepalive requests.
- Edge proxy config: health_check_interval=60s, probe_parallelism=4; persistent connections enabled.
- Dedicated pool autoscaler had a scale event 02:28 due to CPU pressure which may have shifted routing briefly.

Hypotheses: 
1) Double-accounting: the edge proxy increments request counters and origin also increments preflight/health count leading to faster burst depletion.
2) Refill alignment: Short refill window at edge (aligned to minute) vs origin (aligned to epoch boundary) causes sawtooth depletion when flusher jobs are near boundary.
3) Shared API key: background jobs and webhooks sharing token bucket is primary surface area; even if accounting is correct, policy separation would avoid user-visible impact.

Next steps (assigned):
- SRE (Ravi) to pull per-connection accounting traces for the example request IDs and correlate with edge connection IDs.
- Ask customer to isolate a canary API key for webhook traffic so we can prove separation (workaround).
- Engineering: review rate-limiter logic around preflight/keepalive counting for persistent HTTP/2 connections (possible shadow counting).
comments: 2026-03-10 10:12 - Ava Martinez (Support): Reached out to customer to request sample request IDs and console exports. Customer provided three sample windows and the flusher cron schedule.
2026-03-10 13:45 - Ravi Patel (SRE): Confirmed sawtooth pattern in tenant refill graph. Pulling per-conn logs for rq_6a9f2b - ETA 2026-03-12.
2026-03-11 09:02 - Priya Shah (Edge Team): Edge config probe_parallelism=4 noted. Asked if customer can reduce probe concurrency to 1 as short-term mitigant.
2026-03-11 14:30 - Customer (ACME Support Lead, Jordan Li): Agreed to create separate API key for webhooks and run for 24 hours; requested recommended policy settings for burst and sustained rates.

2026-03-12 08:20 - Ravi Patel (SRE): Initial per-connection traces show preflight PINGs counted as requests at origin when probe concurrency >1. Filing internal follow-up with rate-limiter owners (linked PRs).
suggested_workaround: Create separate API key for webhook callbacks; assign webhook key to a policy with isolated burst pool and a slightly higher short-window burst allowance. Temporarily reduce edge probe_parallelism to 1 and stagger background flusher schedules to avoid aligning with refill epoch boundaries.
next_actions: 1) SRE to provide tracing evidence and log extracts (in progress). 2) Support to coordinate with customer on canary key roll and monitor for 24h. 3) Eng to assess preflight/keepalive counting and propose a fix (debounce or dedupe preflight counts).
customer_notes: ACME: Webhook delivery SLA is critical; background flushers can be delayed by up to 10 minutes but cannot cause webhook drops. Prefer configuration guidance over code changes when possible.
